sourcedFrom: Pellet Flintlock Muzzleloader Owner's Manual — PENNSYLVANIA PELLET FLINTLOCK MUZZLELOADER — Fit 40 – 06/02 Jb2 (none printed)
cleanIntro:
This guide follows Traditions's Pennsylvania Pellet Flintlock owner's manual; check your variant against it. The book is written for the PA Pellet flintlock and does not print the word Ultralight, so every step here is stated as generally as the book states it.

The PA Pellet is not a standard sidelock: its breech plug is designed to come out, and Traditions makes taking it out part of the routine strip so the inside of the barrel can be cleaned end to end. Black powder fouling can rust a barrel overnight, so the book asks for a complete cleaning as soon as possible after every shooting session. DEEP CLEAN carries the tang and trigger, the lock out of the stock, and what to do with a breech plug that will not turn.

steps.title: Muzzle up and downrange, nothing over it
steps.action: This guide follows Traditions's Pennsylvania Pellet Flintlock owner's manual; check your variant against it. Keep the muzzle pointed upward and downrange, and keep your face and hands from ever passing over it, whether or not you think the rifle is loaded. A muzzleloader has no action to open and look into, so how you hold it is the first line of safety.
steps.quote: CAUTION: NEVER WORK WITH YOUR FACE OR ANY PART OF YOUR BODY OVER THE MUZZLE, EVEN WHEN THE GUN IS BELIEVED TO BE UNLOADED. ALWAYS KEEP THE MUZZLE OF THE GUN POINTED UPWARD AND DOWNRANGE.
steps.cite: Pellet Flintlock Muzzleloader Owner's Manual — PENNSYLVANIA PELLET FLINTLOCK MUZZLELOADER — Fit 40 – 06/02 Jb2 — LOADING YOUR MUZZLELOADER, printed p.11 (PDF p.9)

steps.title: Frizzen open, pan dumped, hammer at half-cock
steps.action: Open the frizzen, tip the priming powder out of the pan, and bring the hammer back to half-cock. Until the pan is empty the rifle is primed, and the pan is the only place you can see that. With the frizzen forward there is nothing for the flint to strike.
steps.quote: If you decide that you are not going to fire the muzzleloader, you must open the frizzen and dump the priming powder out of the pan and return the hammer into the half-cock position.
steps.cite: Pellet Flintlock Muzzleloader Owner's Manual — PENNSYLVANIA PELLET FLINTLOCK MUZZLELOADER — Fit 40 – 06/02 Jb2 — PRIMING THE MUZZLELOADER, printed p.13 (PDF p.10)

steps.title: A charge in the barrel means the rifle is loaded
steps.action: An empty pan does not make an empty rifle. If a charge is still in the barrel, Traditions counts the rifle as loaded, and this book prints no procedure for pulling a charge, so this guide does not supply one. Only go on to the strip with a barrel you know is uncharged.
steps.quote: CAUTION: IF THERE IS STILL A CHARGE INSIDE THE BARREL, THE MUZZLELOADER IS CONSIDERED LOADED.
steps.cite: Pellet Flintlock Muzzleloader Owner's Manual — PENNSYLVANIA PELLET FLINTLOCK MUZZLELOADER — Fit 40 – 06/02 Jb2 — PRIMING THE MUZZLELOADER, printed p.13 (PDF p.10)
steps.warn: CAUTION: IF THERE IS STILL A CHARGE INSIDE THE BARREL, THE MUZZLELOADER IS CONSIDERED LOADED.

steps.title: Ramrod out, frizzen forward
steps.action: Draw the ramrod out of its thimbles and set it aside, then push the frizzen to its forward, open position. Both come first because the barrel cannot leave the stock with the ramrod under it, and an open frizzen is out of the way of your hands.
steps.quote: Open frizzen to the forward position.
steps.cite: Pellet Flintlock Muzzleloader Owner's Manual — PENNSYLVANIA PELLET FLINTLOCK MUZZLELOADER — Fit 40 – 06/02 Jb2 — DISASSEMBLY — To Remove the Barrel from the Stock, printed p.5 (PDF p.6)

steps.title: Barrel wedge out, from the lock side
steps.action: Drive the barrel tenon wedge out toward the lock side of the stock with a wedge puller or a non-marring punch. Go carefully: the wedge passes through the wood, and a steel punch or a heavy blow marks the stock. Keep the wedge with the ramrod.
steps.quote: Carefully remove the barrel tenon wedge out from the lock side of the stock with a Tradition’s wedge puller or a non-marring punch.
steps.cite: Pellet Flintlock Muzzleloader Owner's Manual — PENNSYLVANIA PELLET FLINTLOCK MUZZLELOADER — Fit 40 – 06/02 Jb2 — DISASSEMBLY — To Remove the Barrel from the Stock, printed p.5 (PDF p.6)

steps.title: Both lock plate screws loosened
steps.action: Loosen both lock plate screws from the lock side. The book says loosen, not remove, at this stage: the barrel is coming out, not the lock. The front screw is also what holds the ramrod retaining spring in the stock.
steps.quote: Loosen BOTH lock plate screws from the side of the lock.
steps.cite: Pellet Flintlock Muzzleloader Owner's Manual — PENNSYLVANIA PELLET FLINTLOCK MUZZLELOADER — Fit 40 – 06/02 Jb2 — DISASSEMBLY — To Remove the Barrel from the Stock, printed p.5 (PDF p.6)

steps.title: Barrel lifted part way, then pulled away from the tang
steps.action: Hold the stock, lift the barrel only part way out of its channel, then draw it forward away from the tang, twisting it back and forth if it resists. The breech end is hooked into the tang. Lift too far before it has come forward and you bend the tang.
steps.caution: Take care not to pull up too much on the barrel or the tang may bend.
steps.quote: Grasp the barrel and the stock with your hands and lift the barrel up part way out of the channel. Pull the barrel away from the tang while holding the stock. You may need to twist the barrel back and forth while you are pulling away. Take care not to pull up too much on the barrel or the tang may bend.
steps.cite: Pellet Flintlock Muzzleloader Owner's Manual — PENNSYLVANIA PELLET FLINTLOCK MUZZLELOADER — Fit 40 – 06/02 Jb2 — DISASSEMBLY — To Remove the Barrel from the Stock, printed p.5 (PDF p.6)

steps.title: Touch hole liner out FIRST
steps.action: Before the breech plug is touched, unscrew the touch hole liner from the side of the barrel with a flat-head screwdriver. Traditions puts this in capitals because the liner sits in the way of the plug. Keep the liner somewhere it cannot roll off the bench.
steps.prose: The quote keeps the maker's spelling 'IMORTANT' as printed.
steps.aside: Use a flathead screwdriver to remove touch hole liner.
steps.quote: IMORTANT: REMOVE TOUCH HOLE LINER FROM SIDE OF BARREL BEFORE UNSCREWING BREECH PLUG.
steps.cite: Pellet Flintlock Muzzleloader Owner's Manual — PENNSYLVANIA PELLET FLINTLOCK MUZZLELOADER — Fit 40 – 06/02 Jb2 — DISASSEMBLY — To Remove the Breech Plug from the Barrel, printed p.6 (PDF p.6)

steps.title: Breech plug out: 6 mm Allen key, counterclockwise
steps.action: Put the 6 mm Allen key that came with the rifle into the breech plug and turn it counterclockwise until the plug comes all the way out of the barrel. This is what the PA Pellet is built for, and it opens the barrel at both ends. If it will not turn, do not lean on it here; the stuck-plug procedure is in DEEP CLEAN.
steps.aside: If you generously lubricate the breech plug threads with Traditions Breech plug grease the chances of getting it stuck after shooting will decrease dramatically.
steps.quote: Turn breech plug counterclockwise until completely removed.
steps.cite: Pellet Flintlock Muzzleloader Owner's Manual — PENNSYLVANIA PELLET FLINTLOCK MUZZLELOADER — Fit 40 – 06/02 Jb2 — DISASSEMBLY — To Remove the Breech Plug from the Barrel, printed p.6 (PDF p.6)

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Barrel out of the stock, touch hole liner out and breech plug out: that is the disassembly Traditions asks for before every complete cleaning. The lock stays in the stock for routine work. The cleaning screens follow; DEEP CLEAN covers the tang and trigger, the lock, and a stuck breech plug.
steps.quote: A complete cleaning of your muzzleloader is to be performed as soon as possible after your shooting session is completed. A complete cleaning is when you will disassemble the muzzleloader to clean and lubricate all parts for the next shooting session, or storage until next season.
steps.cite: Pellet Flintlock Muzzleloader Owner's Manual — PENNSYLVANIA PELLET FLINTLOCK MUZZLELOADER — Fit 40 – 06/02 Jb2 — CLEANING YOUR MUZZLELOADER, printed p.16 (PDF p.11)

steps.title: Breech plug scrubbed, fire channel cleared
steps.action: Scrub the breech plug in hot soapy water with a nylon brush, and pay most attention to the ignition hole and fire channel through it. That channel carries the flash from the pan to the charge, and fouling left in it is a misfire. A pipe cleaner or small bottle brush reaches the narrow parts; dry it completely before any lube goes on.
steps.quote: Clean the breech plug with hot soapy water and a nylon brush. Take care to clean out the ignition and fire channel from fouling or debris.
steps.cite: Pellet Flintlock Muzzleloader Owner's Manual — PENNSYLVANIA PELLET FLINTLOCK MUZZLELOADER — Fit 40 – 06/02 Jb2 — CLEAN & LUBRICATE PARTS — Breech Plug, printed p.7 (PDF p.7)

steps.title: Threads lubed, ignition hole kept dry
steps.action: Coat the breech plug threads with Wonderlube 1000 Plus or Traditions breech plug and nipple grease. Keep every trace of it out of the ignition hole: lube there blocks the flash just as fouling does. Lubed threads are also what stop the plug seizing next time.
steps.quote: Lubricate the threads of the breech plug with Traditions Wonderlube 1000 Plus or Traditions breech plug and nipple grease. Make sure not to put lube in the ignition hole in the breech plug.
steps.cite: Pellet Flintlock Muzzleloader Owner's Manual — PENNSYLVANIA PELLET FLINTLOCK MUZZLELOADER — Fit 40 – 06/02 Jb2 — CLEAN & LUBRICATE PARTS — Breech Plug, printed p.7 (PDF p.7)

steps.title: Muzzle end in a bucket of very hot, soapy water
steps.action: Fill a bucket with four to five inches of very hot, soapy water and stand the barrel in it muzzle end down. With the breech plug out, the barrel is open at both ends and the water can be drawn all the way through. Very hot matters: it shifts black powder fouling, and a hot barrel dries faster.
steps.quote: Fill a bucket with about 4 to 5 inches of very hot, soapy water. Place the muzzle end of the barrel into the cleaning solution.
steps.cite: Pellet Flintlock Muzzleloader Owner's Manual — PENNSYLVANIA PELLET FLINTLOCK MUZZLELOADER — Fit 40 – 06/02 Jb2 — CLEANING YOUR MUZZLELOADER — Complete Cleaning, printed p.17 (PDF p.12)

steps.title: Pump water through the bore with a patched jag
steps.action: Put a patch on the cleaning jag, run the ramrod into the barrel, and pump it so the water is pulled up the bore and pushed back down, over and over, until the bore is clean. A heavily fouled barrel may need a nylon or brass bristle brush first. Keep going until the patches stop coming up dark.
steps.quote: Using your ramrod, place a cleaning patch to the end of the cleaning jag and pump the water up into the barrel repeatedly. Do this until the inside of the bore is clean.
steps.cite: Pellet Flintlock Muzzleloader Owner's Manual — PENNSYLVANIA PELLET FLINTLOCK MUZZLELOADER — Fit 40 – 06/02 Jb2 — CLEANING YOUR MUZZLELOADER — Complete Cleaning, printed p.17 (PDF p.12)

steps.title: Dry patches until the bore is dry
steps.action: Once the bore is clean, run dry patches up and down it until one comes out dry. Then dry the outside of the barrel with a clean cloth and give it a light coat of oil. Water left anywhere on this barrel is rust by morning.
steps.aside: Completely dry exterior of barrel with clean cloth. Lightly oil the outside of the barrel.
steps.quote: When the inside of the barrel is clean, run a dry patch up and down inside the bore until dry.
steps.cite: Pellet Flintlock Muzzleloader Owner's Manual — PENNSYLVANIA PELLET FLINTLOCK MUZZLELOADER — Fit 40 – 06/02 Jb2 — CLEANING YOUR MUZZLELOADER — Complete Cleaning, printed p.17 (PDF p.12)

steps.title: Touch hole picked clear
steps.action: Clear the touch hole with a cleaning pick or a pipe cleaner until nothing is left in it. On a flintlock the spark has to travel through that hole to reach the charge, and the pipe cleaner also dries it out. Do the same to the touch hole liner you took out.
steps.quote: Use a Tradition’s Cleaning pick or a pipe cleaner to clean the touch hole from fouling or debris that may interfere with your next ignition. The pipe cleaner will help dry out the hole.
steps.cite: Pellet Flintlock Muzzleloader Owner's Manual — PENNSYLVANIA PELLET FLINTLOCK MUZZLELOADER — Fit 40 – 06/02 Jb2 — CLEANING YOUR MUZZLELOADER — Field Cleaning, printed p.17 (PDF p.12)

steps.title: Stock channel wiped, ramrod spring checked
steps.action: Wipe the debris out of the barrel channel in the stock with a clean cloth, and watch for small parts while you do. Look at the ramrod retaining spring: it is held by the front lock plate screw, and if it has shifted the ramrod will sit loose once the barrel is back in.
steps.prose: The quote keeps the maker's 'loose' as printed.
steps.quote: Clean off debris inside stock channel with a clean cloth. Take care not to loose any parts inside stock. Check ramrod retaining spring for proper positioning. The ramrod retaining spring is held in place by the front lock plate screw.
steps.cite: Pellet Flintlock Muzzleloader Owner's Manual — PENNSYLVANIA PELLET FLINTLOCK MUZZLELOADER — Fit 40 – 06/02 Jb2 — CLEAN & LUBRICATE PARTS — Stock, printed p.7 (PDF p.7)

deepSteps.title: Tang screw out, and catch the trigger assembly
deepSteps.action: Unscrew the flat-head screw from the tang. The same screw holds the trigger assembly in the stock, so have a hand under it as the screw comes free. Lift the tang and the trigger assembly out and keep them together.
deepSteps.quote: The tang screw also holds the trigger assembly in place. Take care to not drop the trigger assembly when tang is unscrewed.
deepSteps.cite: Pellet Flintlock Muzzleloader Owner's Manual — PENNSYLVANIA PELLET FLINTLOCK MUZZLELOADER — Fit 40 – 06/02 Jb2 — CLEANING YOUR MUZZLELOADER — To Remove the Tang and Trigger Assembly, printed p.17 (PDF p.12)

deepSteps.title: Lock plate screws out, lock out the other side
deepSteps.action: Take both lock plate screws all the way out. The lock comes out from the opposite side of the stock. Work over the bench, because the lock's small parts are easy to lose; mind the ramrod retaining spring, which the front screw was holding.
deepSteps.quote: Lock should come out of the opposite side of the stock.
deepSteps.cite: Pellet Flintlock Muzzleloader Owner's Manual — PENNSYLVANIA PELLET FLINTLOCK MUZZLELOADER — Fit 40 – 06/02 Jb2 — CLEANING YOUR MUZZLELOADER — To Remove Lock and Lock Plate, printed p.18 (PDF p.12)

deepSteps.title: Lock brushed clean, kept dry
deepSteps.action: Brush the lock plate and its parts clean with a double-ended cleaning brush. This part is cleaned dry: keep water and fouling out of the trigger assembly. Then clean the residue out of the stock, inside and out.
deepSteps.quote: Clean the lock plate and parts with a Tradition’s double-ended cleaning brush to remove any debris. Take care not to get any water or fouling inside the trigger assembly.
deepSteps.cite: Pellet Flintlock Muzzleloader Owner's Manual — PENNSYLVANIA PELLET FLINTLOCK MUZZLELOADER — Fit 40 – 06/02 Jb2 — CLEANING YOUR MUZZLELOADER — To Remove Lock and Lock Plate, printed p.18 (PDF p.12)

deepSteps.title: All metal coated, then stored dry and out of a case
deepSteps.action: When every metal part is clean and dry, give it a light coat of Wonderlube 1000 Plus, and coat the bore inside and out. Store the rifle somewhere cool, dry and secured, and not in a gun case, which holds condensation against the steel. For long storage the book asks for a heavier coat of oil.
deepSteps.quote: Store your muzzleloader in a cool, dry secured area. Storage in a gun case is not recommended, as it could produce condensation and corrosion. During long periods of storage a heavier application of oil is recommended.
deepSteps.cite: Pellet Flintlock Muzzleloader Owner's Manual — PENNSYLVANIA PELLET FLINTLOCK MUZZLELOADER — Fit 40 – 06/02 Jb2 — CLEANING YOUR MUZZLELOADER — To Remove Lock and Lock Plate, printed p.18 (PDF p.12)

deepSteps.title: Stuck breech plug: soak the breech end for half an hour
deepSteps.action: If the plug will not turn, take the barrel out of the stock and the touch hole liner out of the barrel, then stand the breech end in very hot, soapy water for half an hour. The heat and water soften the fouling binding the threads. Warm water is not enough.
deepSteps.quote: Fill a bucket with very hot, soapy water as soak breech end of the barrel for 1/2 hour. This will help loosen up the fouling inside the breech area. The water must be very hot to penetrate the fouling and barrel material.
deepSteps.cite: Pellet Flintlock Muzzleloader Owner's Manual — PENNSYLVANIA PELLET FLINTLOCK MUZZLELOADER — Fit 40 – 06/02 Jb2 — RECOMMENDATIONS FOR REMOVING A STUCK BREECH PLUG, printed p.6 (PDF p.6)

deepSteps.title: Stuck breech plug: padded vise, rock it free
deepSteps.action: Brace the barrel in a padded vise and use the 6 mm Allen key. Traditions says you may need to tighten the plug slightly first, then rock it back and forth to break up the fouling in the threads, and that a bar slipped over the key can add leverage. All of this is avoided by lubing the threads before shooting.
deepSteps.quote: Brace the barrel inside a padded vice and use the 6mm allen key supplied. It may be necessary to actually tighten the plug a little and then rock the plug back and forth to loosen up the threads and fouling.
deepSteps.cite: Pellet Flintlock Muzzleloader Owner's Manual — PENNSYLVANIA PELLET FLINTLOCK MUZZLELOADER — Fit 40 – 06/02 Jb2 — RECOMMENDATIONS FOR REMOVING A STUCK BREECH PLUG, printed p.6 (PDF p.6)

deepSteps.title: Flint, liner, mainspring and frizzen are wear parts
deepSteps.action: While the rifle is apart, look over the flint, the touch hole liner, the mainspring and the frizzen. Traditions treats all four as inexpensive parts to replace about once a year, and more often the more you shoot. A worn frizzen or flint is a weak spark.
deepSteps.quote: NOTE: FLINTS, TOUCH HOLE LINERS, MAINSPRINGS AND FRIZZENS ARE RELATIVELY INEXPENSIVE AND SHOULD BE CHANGED FREQUENTLY TO KEEP MUZZLELOADER IN PROPER WORKING ORDER. APPROXIMATELY ONCE A YEAR SHOULD BE ADEQUATE.
deepSteps.cite: Pellet Flintlock Muzzleloader Owner's Manual — PENNSYLVANIA PELLET FLINTLOCK MUZZLELOADER — Fit 40 – 06/02 Jb2 — INSTALLING THE FLINT INTO THE JAWS, printed p.10 (PDF p.8)

cleaning.name: BREECH PLUG
tasks: Scrub the breech plug in hot soapy water with a nylon brush
Clear the ignition and fire channel with a pipe cleaner or small bottle brush
Dry the plug completely before lubing
Lube the threads with Wonderlube 1000 Plus or breech plug and nipple grease
Do not put lube in the ignition hole in the breech plug

cleaning.name: BARREL & BORE
tasks: Stand the muzzle end in 4 to 5 inches of very hot, soapy water
Pump water through the bore with a patched jag until it is clean
Use a nylon or brass bristle brush on heavy fouling
Run dry patches until the bore is dry
Dry the outside of the barrel and oil it lightly

cleaning.name: TOUCH HOLE
tasks: Clear the touch hole with a cleaning pick or pipe cleaner
Clean and dry the touch hole liner before it goes back in

cleaning.name: STOCK & LOCK
tasks: Wipe the debris out of the stock channel
Check the ramrod retaining spring under the front lock plate screw
Light coat of Wonderlube 1000 Plus on all clean, dry metal
Store cool, dry and locked, not in a gun case

reassembly: Lube the breech plug threads if not done yet, screw the plug into the barrel and tighten it with the Allen key, hand-tight, until the two alignment marks line up; that is what lines the flash hole up, and you can look through to check it.
Screw the touch hole liner back into the side of the barrel with a flat-head screwdriver, hand-tight.
If the tang and trigger came out: set the trigger into its cut-out facing the right way, set the tang in, and tighten its screw by hand with a flat-head screwdriver.
Before the barrel goes in, check the ramrod retaining spring hangs behind the front lock plate screw with the open end of the U up, facing the rear of the stock.

Insert the barrel at the same angle it came out, twisting it back and forth into the tang; a rubber mallet can help seat it. Then press it down into the stock until the tenon hole lines up and tap the wedge through from the lock side only.
Tighten both lock plate screws and return the ramrod to its thimbles. A loose ramrod means the retaining spring is out of place and the barrel has to come back out to fix it.
fncheck: With the rifle unloaded and the frizzen open, pull the hammer back to half-cock and push it forward: it must not fall. Pull it to full cock and push forward again: it must not fall. Then pull the trigger and check the hammer falls forward toward the open frizzen. Traditions prints this check as the last step of assembly.
